text: Unless the old goes, new cannot come in. A yogi is always in search of his true identity or consciousness, which means to go beyond all images. Not the images that you see around but images that we build up in our mind
author: Sri M

text: When you are undergoing internal churning, what comes out is the poison stored inside. That is the time you shouldn’t fall or get addicted to it. Instead watch it and let it subside. What will come next is amrita.
author: Sri M

text: The purpose of life is to be fulfilled, to be happy, to move forward, to evolve. However, even if you find that which gives you happiness, you are not satisfied, you want to have more. This movement towards more is actually the movement towards Truth. Because the ultimate satisfaction is found only when one touches the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: Faith can move mountains. Have faith in your essential divinity and you can achieve what looks impossible.
author: Sri M

text: When a person has unquestioned faith in his own capacity for achieving a goal, whether spiritual or temporal, he is not disturbed by negative thoughts that weaken the will & discourage the spirit. He persists in his efforts till the very end and attains what he sets out to do.
author: Sri M

text: Change has to come from within. It cannot be brought from outside.
author: Sri M

text: A quiet, calm mind is like a runway for an airplane to take off.
author: Sri M

text: Inspiration comes when the mind is quiet and tranquil. That's when it renews itself and brings out new ideas, new thoughts and new creative instincts.
author: Sri M

text: Many of our problems exist because we get stuck with what happened in the past. Only when you understand that it is all part of memory, an old recording, can you work to stop it. Understand that it is not taking you even an inch towards the goal of the freedom you seek.
author: Sri M

text: With more and more awareness of one's thoughts and how we actually see ourselves as we are, we begin to understand where to start. If you work inside, the outside will work itself out.
author: Sri M

text: The most important quality that a spiritually inclined person needs is the attitude of ‘Sarvabhuta hite ratah’ - welfare of all living beings in your heart.
author: Sri M

text: There is an energy in all human beings which remains inactive in most cases, and the process of sadhana is that by which this potential energy is awakened. So long as this energy is inactive, it is potential energy. It is converted into active or kinetic energy through sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: Every religion has their individual systems, but what remains the same is the core – finding the Truth. The core principle of all religions is how to refine and transform the mind but the approaches are different.
author: Sri M

text: Tena tyaktena bhunjita – ‘let go and rejoice! Don’t get caught up in this circus. Let go and enjoy yourself – rejoice!
author: Sri M

text: The rishis declare that the reservoir of all enjoyment, which manifests itself in small portions, is all within. You may call it hridaya, you may call it the ‘inner consciousness,’ you may call it atma. It is within!
author: Sri M

text: It's a wondrous journey. I would say treat it like an adventure. When you go for an adventure, you get into so many problems, you don’t stop.
author: Sri M

text: The origin of all things, the source from which we have all come, the entire universe, the cosmos is by nature purna, complete
author: Sri M

text: Everybody is not interested in spiritual practice. You are trying to swim against the stream, it's not a joke. Others who don’t want to dare that, will say this is foolish, it is not going to happen. So don't live your spiritual life based on what other people say.
author: Sri M

text: The whole movement of life and evolution is how to become complete. Why? Because even though we don't realize it, at the back of our mind, we know we have come from that which is complete. So, in essence we are complete and therefore all we do is try to attain that completeness.
author: Sri M

text: Ultimate completeness and happiness or satisfaction can never be achieved as long as the senses are looking for it outside. Only if you turn inwards, perhaps you will hit upon the source.
author: Sri M

text: Upanishads are the essence of Vedic knowledge. They come at the end of the Vedas, therefore they are called Vedanta. They are the jewels of wisdom.
author: Sri M

text: When one realizes the impermanence of life and begins to wonder if there is anything permanent at all, the rishis step in and say ‘There is something permanent and That is You. You don’t have to search for it outside. Your search for happiness is actually the search for this Supreme Isha but in the wrong direction! This wonderful thing is inside you.’
author: Sri M

text: The main qualities that develop in one who has taken to spiritual sadhana is that in time, distractions become less when you meditate on your deity or inner self. The person also begins to have better control over emotions, and it’s easier to do japa or other practices. There is an element of enjoyment in the practice.
author: Sri M

text: In Chandogya Upanishad, the Rish i asks his son when he returns home after his formal education with another Rishi , ‘Have you found the truth?’ The son says ‘I think I have’. To this the father says, “If you think you have, you have Not. Either you have found It or not
author: Sri M

text: Through Yoga, you learn how to calm and quiet your mind and how to balance energies in your system. author: Sri M

text: If you change the attitude of your mind, there is tremendous energy which can be used for good. We don’t allow that tremendous energy to come, by limiting our mind and allowing it to be distracted.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga shastra is the science by which you can touch That Infinite Being by deconditioning the conditioned thought that has been built into our system from birth, or perhaps even before birth, if you believe in past births. To break that conditioning, and prepare the instrument to receive the understanding of the Supreme, you require yoga.
author: Sri M

text: The Bhagavad Gita is the teaching of the Upanishads and Upanishads teach Brahmavidya, the knowledge or understanding of the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: When we practice kriya yoga we are trying to balance the Ida and the Pingala and make the prana flow in the main channel called the Sushumna so that gradually the mind is deconditioned and you open up to greater realities.
author: Sri M

text: In the Gita, Krishna says one who fixes complete attention on me while he lives in this world, is happy and when he goes also, he is happy, because he knows he is reaching me or in essence the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: Peace comes when the mind, even though engaged in action, is not dependent on the result. You cannot do anything without having any aim, or looking for a result but when you do that work, you should understand whatever result comes out of this work, should therefore be offered to the Lord, because the energy that i have, to work, is also given by the Lord.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana of our daily life begins with facing the sorrows that are before us and sorting them out
author: Sri M

text: You can’t retire and go and sit in a cave. Where you stay, can you face the battle, anchoring your mind in the essence of That being?
author: Sri M

text: Sankalpa, or the capacity to visualize is unique to us. We are sharing it with the higher-level beings who have visualized this universe and when you visualize, it later on becomes a reality.
author: Sri M

text: Visualization can be creative or destructive. So we have to be very careful, which is why the yogis have been told to follow certain ground rules of which one is not to cause injury to others. So keep your mind clear and do not cause injury to others.
author: Sri M

text: The most intelligent person soon realizes the limitations of his or her intellect and that there are many things beyond that.
author: Sri M

text: Do not put your thought process in the freezer, use it but understand that what is real transcends thought and you need a sharp intellect to understand this.
author: Sri M

author: Sri M

text: When you meditate, keep your mind like a flame without any wind, no flickering, protected from all winds, which is steady.
author: Sri M

text: The aim of Babaji’s teachings is for you to find your true self.
author: Sri M

text: Don't think of Shunyata as emptiness. It is fullness at its best. It is called emptiness because it is empty of all the ideas of fullness that we have.
author: Sri M

author: Sri M

author: Sri M

text: Reaching the spiritual goal is a matter of effort, it is a matter of time and it is a matter of grace.
author: Sri M

author: Sri M

author: Sri M

text: The breath is a link between your soul, your inner being and your outer body. If you can give attention to your breath, you can slowly move towards that which controls the breath.
author: Sri M

text: As you give attention to the breath, you move towards that which is making your breath move up and down, and when you have touched that, then from there you trace it further to the inner, deeper levels.
author: Sri M

text: The golden rule of yama and niyama is moderation. If you don’t have moderation, you cannot meditate. Everything has to be done in moderate proportions—eating, drinking, entertainment, walking, exercising.
author: Sri M

text: Truthful means to appreciate and encourage that part of reality which is beneficial to all as much as possible. The rishis have said that to be truthful is to be transparent. If you yourself are not truthful, how can you teach truth to someone else?
author: Sri M

text: The framework on which we form our images of this world is based on the inputs and the inputs can vary according to the instrument of perception. Therefore we really don't know what it is.
author: Sri M

text: The whole idea of Vedanta and the search is to find the witnessing entity separated from the conditioned witnessing entity; to the absolute unconditioned entity, the witnessing entity. In Sanskrit it’s called sakshi, the witness.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is actually that which is not, but is ever becoming. When the becoming ceases, there is only that which is.
author: Sri M

text: According to Vedanta, the expression used to describe the ultimate reality, the Supreme Being, whatever the limited mind cannot conceive is called Satchitananda.
author: Sri M

text: Agamas described That happiness as Anantam Anandam Brahma. That Ananda has no Anta, no end. How wonderful! It's all part of you and me. You don't have to depend on anything, but your own self..
author: Sri M

text: Vedanta says that when you derive bliss or happiness from anything, you are merely manifesting a small part of the Ananda of the Supreme Reality.
author: Sri M

text: Vedanta says - Tat Tvam Asi, you are not this you are That. This means the limited individual, that means the unlimited Sat.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is the most important aspect of time. If you like something, time seems to be running very fast. If you don't like something, time seems to be running very slow.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana is living every day as a new day letting go of yesterday
author: Sri M

text: Yogas chitta vritti nirodha, which means yoga is the removal of all the disturbances and contradictions, all the distractions of the mind. When all the distractions of the mind are removed and the mind becomes like a clean mirror, in that quietness and calmness of mind is reflected the True Self.
author: Sri M

text: When you start your sadhana , you are swimming against the stream. Everybody is swimming in one way, you are trying to turn around and swim in the opposite direction. So, naturally obstacles and problems start coming before you, especially when it intensifies. That is the time when you must say, ‘Okay, I’m not going to let go of this. I will move forward. I will not get defeated, I need to win.’
author: Sri M

text: Every human being, whatever be the outward actions or behavior, deep within treasures the Shivam , the Supreme Being. So, treat all human beings as temples, sacred. This is the first lesson to learn, moving forward in your sadhana . Otherwise you can sit and meditate for 6 hrs, if you don’t learn this, nothing moves.
author: Sri M

text: Damru is special to Shiva. Dhug, dhug, dhug, when you make the sound of the damru and the nagada , you are sending a message to those beings who are responsible for the Jyotirlinga, saying we remember, keep an eye on us, what you gave us, we are treating with great respect.
author: Sri M

text: The Yogi knows that the first thing you hear in the Anahata, when the mind becomes calm, quietly enjoying, contemplating on the inner Shivam, is dum, dum, dum , the damru. Normally you don’t hear because you are so engrossed in the gross sounds of the outside. Deep inside it is dum, dum, dum, the damru. Which means it’s a signal that the Yogi is moving towards the light, the Jyoti.
author: Sri M

text: Trishool that Shiva holds - central part is the sushumna, right is the Pingala and left is the Ida nadi. When the Yogi symbolises the Trishool , it’s the spinal cord, the sushumna. And there is a damru tied as well, which is the internal sound that you hear when Ida - Pingala is balanced, and your energy is rising in the Sushumna, through the middle.
author: Sri M

text: Har Har Mahadev! Har means hara - to finish, to destroy, to remove and when everything is removed, who stays? Mahadev, who is in each one of us. So, the aim of sadhana is to find Shiva in yourself.
author: Sri M

text: Do go at least once to the temple and see the aarti. If you can’t do that, sit quietly and meditate on the Shivam within you. Ajna is the doorway. When you look there, the light appears and, in this light, you see the Shivam which is residing in the Sahasrara. You are filled with bliss because Shivam also means Anandam.
author: Sri M

text: The night of Shivaratri is supposed to be the day of Shiva. What is night to us, is the day to the deity. It’s an awakening of energies and at that time if you sit down and do your sadhana, it will be very effective. This is why it is called the night of Shiva.
author: Sri M

text: Shiva is neither born, nor does he die. As they say in Kashmir Shaivism, Shivam is Parabrahman, the all-pervading reality.
author: Sri M

text: The moment I begin to say that I have reached the Truth, I have actually not reached the truth. Because when there is the Truth, I am not there.
author: Sri M

text: In meditation, the more you go towards that which is nothing, because we cannot define it, the more things happen. We are going towards the ultimate, ‘Shunya’, which doesn’t mean nothing. It means - not a thing.
author: Sri M

text: Asanas and pranayama help to bring changes in you so that not only you are physically healthy, but also your mind becomes calm.
author: Sri M

text: Mantra Japa is meant primarily for the mind and that which is beyond the mind. Because only when the mind becomes completely free of its distractions, then only it gets the tarmac to go to higher levels of spiritual consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: In life, every action has to have a reaction. It has to go according to the karmic movement.
author: Sri M

text: Atma Sakshatkara is rather difficult to define. It’s an unending process and the starting point is when you actually understand that you are not this body.
author: Sri M

text: Jnana is a very important aspect. Education is not about getting degrees and just getting marks and good jobs. It’s actually to help to flower the mind.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot be free of something until you have understood it.
author: Sri M

text: To understand ignorance means to understand the implications of the meaning of ignorance. And when you have understood that, you are free of death. When you have understood that the Supreme Being which pervades everything, which pervades the entire universe, is no different from your Self, then there is no death for you.
author: Sri M

text: When the ‘little ego,’ the ‘little I’ is done with and becomes still, then the ‘greater I’ manifests itself.
author: Sri M

text: The inner essence does not end with the end of the physical body. It remains forever in its own essential bliss.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishadic way of exploring consciousness is through concrete examples, symbols and tangible things, with which you can kind of understand the intangible and having theoretically understood about the intangible, able to transcend our ordinary mind and perhaps go beyond.
author: Sri M

text: Dialogue is when both participate equally; thinking here is a problem, let us solve it together.
author: Sri M

text: The Keno Upanishad comes from the Sama Veda and from the point of view of the Vedantic studies, the Sama Veda is a very important Veda, because all the music that we have in India comes from the Sama Veda .
author: Sri M

text: The Mandukya Upanishad explains AUM as consisting of Aa, Uu and Mm , of which Aa is the waking state, Uu is the dream state and Mm is the deep sleep and Mm as it ends, unsaid unstruck sound is turiya . The Upanishad says that turiya is your true essence. When you have discovered that, you have discovered the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says, when you find the Truth, you find that there is one Truth, it pervades everything. It’s complete, it doesn’t diminish, it’s always there.
author: Sri M

text: To become spiritual is not to put your brain in the freezer. Think, find out for yourself, because when you find out for yourself it’s your understanding not mine. If you accept what I am saying, it’s second-hand.
author: Sri M

text: ‘Think out of the box’, don’t go on only linear logic, use fuzzy logic and you will see things which are quite different. The mindset should be unprejudiced and then only enquiry starts.
author: Sri M

text: Spirituality is basically the inner and deeper aspect of religion.
author: Sri M

text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said, 'Blessed are the pure in heart for they shall see God'. He did not say that they will not see God because they belong to this or that community. He said - 'Blessed are the pure in heart.' - doesn't matter who - 'for they shall see God.
author: Sri M

text: For the spiritual quest it is not necessary to get detached from social relations completely. In fact it’s only while living in this world, within your social relationships, that you can actually discover who you are and where you stand.
author: Sri M

text: The whole world is my family. Lokah samastah sukhino bhavantu, may the whole world be happy.
author: Sri M

text: Today’s education basically is quite linear. What we need is, education which is not a supply of information, but something by which the mind becomes sensitive and charged to look at things in a non-linear way.
author: Sri M

text: When all going and grasping and grouping stops, when the mind becomes still, then you touch that which is real.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad describes beautifully that the essence of Truth that you seek, Tad Doore Tadvantike , is far and yet it’s so near. Somebody described, ‘it is nearer to you than your own jugular vein’. So if it is the spiritual truth that you seek, then the linear logic has to be dropped.
author: Sri M

text: Success is not measured by growth of wealth or number of cars or houses. Wealth is measured by the richness of your mind. If the mind is not rich, is poor, whatever you have you are a beggar.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot have compassion for the world, unless you are fully satisfied with yourself. If you are not fully satisfied, what will you give? When my mind is full, I am filled with compassion, then I will look at the outside world.
author: Sri M

text: All the intellectual discussions in the Upanishads, finally boil down to the fact that there is an inner being who is palpably alive in all hearts, and is in essence part of the all-pervading Supreme Being. You may call it Brahman, Narayana or Shivam.
author: Sri M

text: Upanishad takes you through the intellectual maze to crystal clear sanctity which is full of love and affection.
author: Sri M

text: Shruti is something that is heard. Not what is studied, taken home and commented upon and discussed. Shruti is pure sound and therefore Vedas declared that the Shruti is the original voice of the truth. Therefore, when the student is perfectly prepared, Shruti once said it is enough. There is no more need to attend the talks.
author: Sri M

text: The whole exercise is to make the mind so sensitive that when the Shruti strikes, it has its effect. All sadhana is done for that.
author: Sri M

text: If my mind’s frequency and your mind’s frequency is operating at the same levels, words are not required. When the Shruti is heard, it immediately registers.
author: Sri M

text: The infinite truth according to the Upanishads is ‘Tad dure tad vantike’ - It is far, and it is so near.
author: Sri M

text: As you progress, you will become more and more morally perfect and so also will your meditation become better. This will go on until you reach your final goal. Till then, there are bound to be imperfections. Only when one has perfectly understood that all that exists is the 'Self', will selfishness be completely destroyed.
author: Sri M

text: If someone promises salvation for all at once, take care; you are about to be hoodwinked. If someone guarantees to lead you to Supreme Bliss in a certain number of days, again, be on guard. No human being can ensure it; only God can.
author: Sri M

text: All joys spring forth from within your being. The reservoir of all joy, the essence of all bliss, is in your own heart, in the core of your own being.
author: Sri M

text: One of the greatest obstacles to Truth is sloth. Work prevents sleep and sloth.
author: Sri M

text: It's only when there is pain and sorrow that human beings begin to think there may be a divine being somewhere. Guru Nanak Sahib said, ‘ Dukh me sumiran sab kare, sukh me kare na koi (Everyone beseech the Almighty when they are sad, but no one remembers when they are happy).
author: Sri M

text: The relationship between the teacher and the taught is an intimate one – of attitude and mind. I may not meet someone or answer emails but that doesn’t mean that I am not in touch with you. Once you have started on the spiritual journey, you are always on the teacher’s radar.
author: Sri M

text: When I go deep into the core of my consciousness, my capacity to break the bonds with the past expands & I learn to break the fetters one by one. I begin to understand I am not just a conditioned human being with a physical body but perhaps a little more than that.
author: Sri M

text: When a person is on the spiritual journey, he should not cry over what he loses. What he loses may be the stepping-stone to what he is going to gain, which is communion with the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: To move forward, we have to first realise that we are incomplete. And that means humility – to know this is where I stand.
author: Sri M

text: The infinite truth according to the Upanishads is ‘Tad dure tad vantike’ - It is far, and it is so near.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual aspirant in today’s world needs openness to learning, humility and a true desire to look beyond this life.
author: Sri M

text: The outer Dhuni is symbolic of the inner fire of desire for spiritual fulfillment. It cannot be doused easily, once sparked. This is the fire we should light in our hearts.
author: Sri M

text: Some mantras, sounds and words have the capacity to penetrate even deep sleep. If something really enters into your deep sleep, then you can be sure your entire personality has changed.
author: Sri M

text: Let go of all your narrow little ideas practically, and let go of the philosophical understanding that we are separate. Let go of this feeling that I am different and you are different and we are separate.
author: Sri M

text: Miracles can happen if only you can change the attitude of your mind and implement your resolutions.
author: Sri M

text: Someone who has touched the core of one's being becomes a tranquil and a blissful person. But if you are still jealous, angry or irritated, then you have not touched it.
author: Sri M

text: If you want to delve deep into the layers of your consciousness and finally reach the essence, then meditation is a must!
author: Sri M

text: When the breath is slow, prana is slow, when prana is slow, the mind is slow, when prana is very quiet, then the mind becomes absolutely quiet. In that quietness, comes the understanding of your real being.
author: Sri M

text: Fear and depression are of no use to a human being. At turning points in life, have faith in the inner reality which resides in your heart and move forward.
author: Sri M

text: The best way to deal with ego is to gradually and repeatedly understand that you are the actual problem. If you can deal with it, then you can deal with anything.
author: Sri M

text: To lead a good life, we must help as many people as possible, sing the name of God, do our japa' and dwell on the Inner Spirit constantly.
author: Sri M

text: Enjoyment in this world should not be the main aim of life. We should try to do good things, help others. Then the mind begins to become better and more spiritual. It experiences that joy, which you cannot experience anywhere in this world.
author: Sri M

text: While we have a physical body and we live in the physical world, the true essence of our being is the atma , the inner self. All attempts to touch That, to go to the core of yourself, which is an amsha of the Supreme Being, is spirituality.
author: Sri M

text: Karma Yoga is essential for every human being. It is Karma but when the work is done not only for oneself but for others, it becomes Karma Yoga. Otherwise it is only Karma.
author: Sri M

text: When people begin to realize that this life is so temporary. I am here today and gone tomorrow. When they ask is there something permanent, then only the spiritual journey will begin.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says - Atmano mokshartham jagat hitayacha . Moksha for the Atman but do good for the world. You cannot meditate for 24 hours. So, what do you do the rest of the time? Help people. Do work. Look after the world. Only through selfless work does the mind get purified to meditate
author: Sri M

text: In the modern way of life, giving up everything and going away somewhere doesn't work. You will come back in 10 days. Ramakrishna Paramahamsa used to call it monkey’s vairagya.
author: Sri M

text: If there is an effect, it has a cause. This is the karmic theory. IfI have done some karmas in the past and I am suffering the results today, I can't go back to my past birth and change it. What do I have? The present, now! So, self-effort is necessary because that is the only thing you have now.
author: Sri M

text: I think whatever tools are given to us, we must use them to make a better tomorrow rather than saying it will happen, or if it happens, it's my karma, so I'm suffering. You have to wake up.
author: Sri M

text: If you look at life and say this is what I need rather than what I want, then perhaps that is a more effective prayer.
author: Sri M

text: Giving respect to women is a very important part of civilization. If it is not there, no civilization is going to grow or expand. You may economically become rich, but it is of no use. You might culturally still be beggars.
author: Sri M

text: If the mind can stay peaceful, content and ‘ sarvatra samabhudaya’ - tranquil under all circumstances. It is a deliberate process. You cannot expect it to happen. Then the mind becoming quiet and calm reflects on the cells of the body also.
author: Sri M

text: Sat means reality. The truth, the actual, opposite of ‘Asat’ - not true, not reality. Very often we look at ‘Asat’ and think that it is ‘Sat.’ What we think is real may not be real. And what we think is not real, because we cannot see it tangibly, may be real. So, ‘Sat’ means Truth without frills and the reality which is the opposite of that which is not real.
author: Sri M

text: Learn to see things in a new light. Allow the new rays to come in.
author: Sri M

text: Cultivate Sat-sangha, to keep Dur-Sangha away. When people come together, who desire spiritual development, who are simple and good, who don't want to hurt others, who don't want to create problems, who have either reached a spiritual level or are trying to reach a spiritual level, it becomes a sadhu satsanga.
author: Sri M

text: If you don't have a satsanga, there is always a danger of dursangha, because we cannot live alone without communication, without meeting others, because we are society.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t think that to be spiritual is to be meek. You have to be robust before you can walk on this path.
author: Sri M

text: Truth is not meant for the weak. It's a message of inner and quiet strength. Do not be discouraged. Say, whatever discouragement comes on the way I am going to handle it and move forward.
author: Sri M

text: Dialogue is not fighting or argument. Argument is a fight because I have already decided that I am saying the right thing. You have also decided that you are saying the right thing. There is a clash. Dialogue on the other hand is Samvada - you and I are looking at a problem together and trying to solve it.
author: Sri M

text: If you have to learn from the teacher, you cannot go to the teacher and say, hey I am right. It doesn't work. You have to go with an open mind saying, ‘let me understand, please can you make me understand, I want to learn’.
author: Sri M

text: The best principle of cleanliness is not to dirty your mind with bad thoughts about others. In every human being's heart, there is a divine spark. Therefore, we are all equal in that way. We are all walking, talking, speaking, thinking temples of God, because that God is the ‘antaryami,’ the spark of the divine absolute being who exists in our hearts.
author: Sri M

text: Divinity exists in every human being. There is nowhere it does not. On the ultimate side it is ‘Ishavasyam idam sarvam,’ it pervades everywhere, but where we can be conscious of it is, in our hearts.
author: Sri M

text: Is there something which cannot be changed, which is not a dream, which is real, which I need not worry about it going away from me, something which is in essence my own essence? When I have found that, then I am supremely happy, I am free, I am totally self-reliant, I know that the spark of the divine is in my heart and my Atma is a spark of the Paramatma. .
author: Sri M

text: Going within means for some time to stop all external movements and retire, into yourself.
author: Sri M

text: While you have to look after your body to keep it in shape physically and mentally, you should have this understanding that one day this is going to go. So, let me also keep my eye on something which won’t go. That’s the starting point; you have to start there.
author: Sri M

text: Shanti starts from the mind of the individual, from the heart of the matter. If our minds and hearts are at peace, then we can talk about peace, bring about peace, we can get people together. As long as inside we are not peaceful, it's not possible to bring it about to the external.
author: Sri M

text: Don't consider yourself to be limited to individuals. Your potential is unlimited. If you somehow find out the mechanism to touch the unlimited, use it for the entire universe. May everybody be happy.
author: Sri M

text: Dialogue is when you and I decide, here is a problem, let's attempt together to find out. The other is an argument.
author: Sri M

text: A good student becomes a good teacher. And a good teacher is one who knows or who understands that the students also know something which he/she may not know.
author: Sri M

text: Jealousy, anger, fear, affection - these emotions may be different for different people, but the common factor is that we all have it. Spend time on growing yourself, instead of being jealous.
author: Sri M

text: There is only one mind. If I change one part of the mind, it has to affect the other part of the mind. So the change has to begin with me.
author: Sri M

text: If we think that in this vast universe, there is only this Earth, which is like a speck of sand in the ocean, on the shores, we must be really limiting our thought process.
author: Sri M

text: Do not have hatred for anyone to that level that you do not see the good qualities in the person. There may be something. There is no human being who does not have some good quality in life.
author: Sri M

text: Sage Kabir said, ‘Moko kahan dhunde re bande, main to tere paas me’ - where are you searching for me, my dear? I am here right with you.
author: Sri M

text: If you are tranquil and peaceful in yourself then the peacefulness can be shared with others.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad says if you want to understand the Supreme Reality that pervades everywhere, you need to let go' and move away from your own 'small' centre. Expand, let everyone be a part of you.
author: Sri M

text: The ancient teachers said that there is a link between your breathing pattern and emotional states, and if you change the rhythm or pattern of your breath, you can change your emotional state. You can change your mood.
author: Sri M

text: You can learn theories, Vedanta, Tantra, Sankhya, all the Shastras, but unless there is a change in the mindset, there is no possibility of understanding what is being said, because the average mind, which is stuck in its own images, and its own system of thought processes is not ready to touch that which is beyond the grasp of even the senses. So the mind has to be opened and de-conditioned and sadhana is the way to do it.
author: Sri M

text: Please remember that not just the practice, but the determination and intention to find what you're seeking is as important. Otherwise one doesn't move ahead.
author: Sri M

text: Even if you practice any kriya, you need to have the one-pointed desire and devotion to find the Truth. Otherwise, it's simply a mechanical practice.
author: Sri M

text: The word ‘kriya’ in Sanskrit simply means ‘a technique’. This is to decondition your mind which has been brought up in a very conditioned way, through influences, through birth, through various factors, even genetically.
author: Sri M

text: At some point in our lives, we are all faced with sorrow, there is nobody who does not. The sorrow that comes to us is actually an indication that this is not the be-all and end-all of life. There is something more. But we tend either to ignore it or cover it up or entertain ourselves so that we don’t feel it and never face it.
author: Sri M

text: Meditation is how to decondition your mind so you see things as they are. If you see things as they are, you see only one and that is the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: All enquiry starts when you say, I don't know, I need to find out. The moment you say i know, there is no enquiry, it's all over.
author: Sri M

text: Shraddha is a very difficult word to define in English, as it is a Sanskrit word. . Shraddhā means one-pointed attention, it could mean faith, discriminative thinking, any one of these things, or all of them put together.
author: Sri M

text: Your body, mind, subtle body, comes and goes, birth after birth, but the inner essence which is the Atman always remains the same.
author: Sri M

text: Don't identify your Atman with your mind, which gathers things, then loses them, has pain and sorrow. The Atman is Satchidananda, which means it is Sat, Truth, Chit is consciousness and Ananda is bliss, which means that it is intrinsically blissful and doesn't need anything from outside to make it blissful because it is bliss itself.
author: Sri M

text: Ananda is Happiness, bliss, not the bliss that is here today and gone tomorrow, but as the Tantra defines, Anantam Anandam Brahma, unending bliss is Brahman, that which never ends, which has no beginning.
author: Sri M

text: Even if we practice sadhana, it all depends on our intentions, our priorities, how serious we are with it and so on. You can do Kriya and have a good healthy life. You can have a good healthy body and a healthy mind but if that's all that you want, that's also possible. There may rarely be people who want to go beyond and figure out what is the essence of things.
author: Sri M

text: The bliss and the fragrance that you seek is in your heart, inside. If you would only turn around and look within.
author: Sri M

text: In the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, yoga is defined as Yogas Chitta Vritti Nirodha. Chitta means the mind, but when you say vritti it means the mind with both its positive and negative thoughts. If you can balance the mind and remove all the distractions, tensions, contradictions, the mind becomes quiet, absolutely quiet. And a calm mind is very essential to go into the higher levels of yoga. This is not just a mental process. It's also how you live on this earth. You cannot live a violent life and sit to meditate for half an hour and say that my mind is free of distractions, not possible. So, Yoga is a way of life.
author: Sri M

text: All human beings have three gunas, attributes - Sattva, Rajas and Tamo guna. Different people have different proportions of these. Some have one more, some have one less.
author: Sri M

text: In sattva guna there is a quietness and a tranquility which is not inaction but tranquility in action. That means even if you are doing any activity which of course goes under the Rajoguna category, you still are at peace, in Sattva. This is what should be cultivated for most people.
author: Sri M

text: Simplify your possessions. Try to be as simple as possible, because when it is too complicated, your mind cannot be still and you cannot meditate.
author: Sri M

text: In deep meditation, you are required to keep the spine straight for the simple reason that the naadi or the channel of spiritual evolution in the human system flows through the sushumna, which is in the middle of the spine, connecting the sahasrara to the mooladhara.
author: Sri M

text: Most of the back and spinal problems are because we slouch or lean too much. If we can practice sitting straight, many of these problems won't start at all.
author: Sri M

text: When the breath is adjusted in certain rhythmic patterns you are also able to arrange your prana and apana which is the up-going and down-going breath, in a certain rhythm which is required for meditation. For different kinds of meditation, different rhythms are required.
author: Sri M

text: If you slow down and quieten your breath, your mind also quietens down and becomes tranquil.
author: Sri M

text: Stability of mind - to be able to withstand all circumstances equally and tranquilly. Sthitha Prajna is the first proof that we are moving forward. Otherwise you may see numerous visions but if you are still the same person then one is not moving forward.
author: Sri M

text: From the highest point of view, when everything is eliminated, neti neti, what remains is the Truth. That which cannot be negated any more.
author: Sri M

text: Satori means moksha according to Zen terminology. Freedom!
author: Sri M

text: Peace and harmony in this country is very important because I believe that this country is among the nations, a place where people from all over the world have come to get wisdom, peace and happiness.
author: Sri M

text: All the great teachers of all religions have said that the source of all life is one. So uniting human beings together is our priority.
author: Sri M

text: Bijakshara means certain sounds have the potency of bringing about the growth of certain characteristics, especially on the spiritual side. They are like sowing the seed. It depends upon the climate and how you look after the seed that it grows into a beautiful tree.
author: Sri M

text: 108 is considered a mystical number from ancient times because it is a multiple of nine. Nine is one number in this whole system, which, however big it becomes, you multiply nine with any number and if you add the total, it will still remain as nine. It is a symbol of that supreme Shakti or energy, which always remains constant, which can neither be subtracted nor reduced nor added.
author: Sri M

text: Chanting has a certain taste that comes over the years as you chant. Once you begin to have that taste, you will not want to stop chanting.
author: Sri M

text: Ekam Sat Vipra Bahudha Vadanti There is only one truth, but the wise may call it by different names.
author: Sri M

text: You can change somebody through love rather than through hatred. Hatred brings fear. Out of fear if you change, when the fear is removed, it's gone. It should come from within.
author: Sri M

text: The grace of the Supreme is such that touching it can happen to anybody at any time. There are no rules or formulations for that.
author: Sri M

text: Nobody has ever attained the Supreme through sadhana. Sadhana is done to clean the mind. If the Lord wants to enter, you need space. So the mind has to be open.
author: Sri M

text: As Krishna says in the Gita, when the mind becomes sarvatra sama buddhaya, tranquil at all times, and under all circumstances, then the Shruti that is heard immediately has its effect.
author: Sri M

author: Sri M

text: What you see of the world is the image of the world presented to us by the five senses from which the data is gathered and so the mind manufactures what you think is real.
author: Sri M

text: Both in the waking state and dream state, there is a witness. That witness is real, it is always seeing, always reacting. Without that witness there can neither be a waking state nor dream state.
author: Sri M

text: The teaching is more important than the teacher.
author: Sri M

text: When a teacher gives you instructions, follow those instructions completely. Don't say that 'this I'll follow, this I won't'. Therefore to take a Guru - spiritual teacher, as a guide, is a choice that we have to make very carefully.
author: Sri M

text: It is very difficult to comprehend the Guru. It is very difficult to understand because the ways of a spiritual teacher, who is connected with the universe are strange and different. Because we like to always project our images, our thoughts and hope that the Guru will fall in line.
author: Sri M

text: The function of the Guru is to show you a clean mirror and at the right angle so that you can see yourself as you actually are, not what you want to be.
author: Sri M

text: The moment you are serious that nothing else is more important to you than finding the Truth; your Guru will come to you. One of the main functions of the Guru is to make you stand on your own feet.
author: Sri M

text: Merely by taking flowers and gifts to a Guru, one should not suppose that one is moving towards one's spiritual goal. That can happen only when teachings are followed and one remains with the teacher to understand what he is trying to teach and consciously try to change one’s life according to his instructions.
author: Sri M

text: The word Guru has two syllables, Gu and Ru. Gu is Guhya, hidden, dark, darkness and Ru is a short form of Rudra, the destroyer of darkness. So Guru means one who destroys the darkness. When you say Guru, you are not only talking about your physical Guru, you are also talking about the essence of all teachers.
author: Sri M

text: The Guru teaches you how to reach this freedom, how to swim towards it, how to enjoy it, how to discover this ocean within you, and that the ocean is you but you don’t know it.
author: Sri M

text: Every sadhak who goes onto the spiritual path has great difficulties. But if you are serious about it, as serious as you are about making money or having a child then it's not as difficult. The aspiration is important. One has to develop that kind of drid nishchaya , strong desire to find the truth.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana, is meant to purify the mind, to bring about that state which recognises the eternally free. Once it is recognised, then you are eternally free, you don't have any temptations because you have touched the treasure house of all happiness, bliss and satisfaction. There is nothing more to be satisfied.
author: Sri M

text: One need not have fear. Sometimes that becomes an obstacle to moving forward. One thinks what will happen then? Nothing will happen. Everything will happen as it should happen, not what you thought will happen. Keep that in mind.
author: Sri M

text: The whole attempt of sadhana is to bring one There and then break the mold, not before that.
author: Sri M

text: A process of evolution has been set up. Everything works according to that. The setter-up of that evolution is none other than the Supreme Being. When you have finally found the essence of your being, you will realize that you are the maker of destiny. Till then you think somebody is making all this.
author: Sri M

text: If two people who live together are interested in the spiritual field, it is the best, because both of you can complement each other. When you go wrong, she can help, when she goes wrong, you can help. You can practice spiritual sadhana together.
author: Sri M

text: Guru Mantra is the mantra given by one's Guru to the disciple, which means it connects or links you to the Guru.
author: Sri M

text: A true Guru does not want you to be dependent on anybody. He wants you ultimately to flower, become free and not to bind you even to himself.
author: Sri M

text: The Supreme Guru is the Supreme Being and that Supreme Being is all-pervading : Isha Vasyam Idam Sarvam.
author: Sri M

text: People who have touched that have come back and done tremendous work in this world which a person who has not touched it has not been able to do. This is because that Supreme Reality functions through the person in any way it wants. It may not be in what you would have thought you should function, it functions in a different way.
author: Sri M

text: Real intelligence comes when one has the spiritual experience of the Supreme, whichever way one went into it. When then the mind opens up, you see things which you cannot see otherwise.
author: Sri M

text: Sri Vidya is a mantra shastra that teaches you the Beejaksharas meant to awaken the Shakti inside you, the all-pervading Shakti, which also is in us. This is Sri Vidya. It should be learnt from a proper teacher and the teacher should find out if you are qualified or not, not the student.
author: Sri M

text: Having sexual energy is not a bad thing. It means you are healthy. Sadhana is meant to turn that energy into spiritual energy. The Tejas that you have, should be turned into ojas.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot get rid of sorrow unless you face it. If you understand the reason, then you can be free of it forever.
author: Sri M

text: The spiritual path happens to be narrow, not because of any narrowness in thinking but because the other paths are so wide and inviting that it is very tempting to go off on those paths, so much so that they are all highways. In contrast, this little path going up, maybe is a pugdandi raasta!
author: Sri M

text: The source from which a teaching comes can be different. The essence of the teaching is more important.
author: Sri M

text: All the great sages who have gone deep into the question, "Who am I?" have found that as they begin to enquire into the origin of the l', the little, limited I', with which most people identify themselves, disappears because it never ever existed and was merely a product of thought.
author: Sri M

text: As long as ‘I am' there, there is no That. When That is there, ‘I am' is not. Therefore, there are no 'two' anymore but only one.
author: Sri M

text: There is no human being who can live without an attachment. However, when you get more attached to your inner reality, you get more detached from the outer realities. The inner becomes more important and you experience something joyful within. Then you are free.
author: Sri M

text: Everything that exists in this world is constantly in motion. What is here today is not here tomorrow. Nothing that keeps changing and is temporary can be real. Reality is permanent, eternal. The only unchanging, undecaying reality is Brahman.
author: Sri M

text: It is when the inner being becomes happy, that the world becomes full of joy for us. Every little thing, though previously unnoticed, begins to impart a superior joy.
author: Sri M

text: Nirvana is not a state where you are in a trance all the time. Nirvana is when you are free while you are eating, drinking, talking, but you don't have any pretensions, when you don't have anything to hide, or you are not insecure in any way. You are free. That is the beginning of freedom.
author: Sri M

text: To enquire about the Absolute, you should have freedom from the very beginning. It doesn't come at the end. If you can enquire in freedom, then you will end up in freedom. If you enquire in bondage, you will end up in bondage; you might think it is freedom.
author: Sri M

text: Does freedom happen in stages? I would say, it's like the wheel; the network of illusion is gradually lifted as one goes deeper and deeper into understanding one's own self, one's own mind.
author: Sri M

text: During meditation, it is impossible to control your thoughts and make them disappear. Because the moment you try to make them disappear, you are thinking.
author: Sri M

text: In matters of inner exploration, the most important thing is to keep your slate clean.
author: Sri M

text: If we can voluntarily extricate ourselves from the conditioning thoughts that are in our minds and open up for receiving what is beyond the three dimensional world and the ordinary way of thinking, perhaps we can tap the infinite potential that is waiting for us inside our own minds
author: Sri M

text: Life moves. The problem is we would like to freeze it and hold on to it. It is not possible. You can freeze it for a while, seemingly, but it will break its dam and begin to flow again.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna represents love. Love is a comprehensive panacea for all ills. If you really understand the meaning of it – utter selflessness, not love for my own sake but love for Love’s sake – only then, it is a panacea for all problems. This is very rare.
author: Sri M

text: The most important thing for a human being, I believe, is not to cause pain to other human beings. In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna tells Arjuna that one of the most important qualities of my bhakta , devotee is 'sarva bhoota hitey rataha' - compassion for all beings.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna is depicted mostly with a flute in his hand, playing beautiful music. Music penetrates the heart. When you listen to music in rapt attention, you go so deep that you begin to hear the inner music being played all the time.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna is also called Navanita Chor – one who steals the butter, which is derived by churning the milk. Hence, churning is essential, without which nothing can come out. And, when the butter comes out? Krishna steals it and runs away. So, where are ‘You’? Nowhere. If you think on these lines even for a few minutes, you realize – for a short while – you are transported into a joyous life with nothing to worry about.
author: Sri M

text: Music cannot be played if the flute is filled with muck. You have to empty it out. It has to be hollow. You can’t blow through a solid flute. So, all the muck has to go and when it is clean, hand it over to Him. Krishna will play delightful music.
author: Sri M

text: In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna tells Arjuna that the mind can be a friend, but the same mind can also be an enemy. Cultivate the friendly side of your mind. And, don’t give too much attention to the enemy.
author: Sri M

text: If an intense desire to be free of suffering arises in a human mind, that mind need not be an extraordinary intellectual.The intensity of desire to get out of it is mainly emotional, not intellectual. When that feeling comes, then one can completely direct oneself towards the way by which one can be free.
author: Sri M

text: Ninety percent of the troubles in this world are caused by not talking responsibly. Before you speak, follow three principles. What am I going to say? Who am I going to say this to? Is this the right situation? Truth, sometimes, is double-edged. It could hurt and cause problems. So be careful, even if one is speaking the truth.
author: Sri M

text: As long as you have a physical body, nobody can know everything. We need to learn. At any time, one should be prepared to learn.
author: Sri M

text: Samadhi is an altered state of consciousness where the mind becomes absolutely still. all the distractions, opposing thoughts, aggressive thoughts, attaching thoughts subside and you are in a quiet state of an unruffled, waveless pond.
author: Sri M

text: When you reach a state of complete fulfillment in yoga, when you become a proper yogi, you will find that you cannot then be arrogant, it's not possible. author: Sri M

text: The science of yoga says that there are ways and means to gather together prana which is haphazardly wandering around your body and bring it to a certain position.
