text: From the yogic point of view, there are three nadis in us which are the most important among the hundreds, the Ida, the Pingala and the Sushumna.
author: Sri M

text: Freedom is the aim. stand on your own feet. The Atman which is in me is also in you. In time when you find That you will require no help or support. You will be free. So you can sit at your home itself and do your sadhana and reach there. When help is required it will come in some way or the other. Keep this in mind.
author: Sri M

text: You are a product of many lives, and therefore don't measure your progress against somebody else. Pace is different for different people.
author: Sri M

text: The basic meaning of the word yoga is to open up the mind and bring to the fore all the potential that you have locked in somewhere
author: Sri M

text: Yoga says that the essence of the mind is free of tension, of the ups and downs that we all experience in life. When the mind is absolutely quiet, when all the vrittis have been removed,, in that quietness comes intelligence, buddhi which leads you to the Atman and your expanded mind has such infinite potential you wouldn't have dreamt of.
author: Sri M

text: A person who is really intelligent, is one who grasps without prejudice. Such a mind develops infinite potential because it is not conditioned by all the information that one has gathered over the years. It is crystal clear because it's only when the mind is crystal clear that it can grasp.
author: Sri M

text: The aim of chanting is not to chant, but to bring about silence. One need not mistake the technique to be the goal. If the goal is felt, stop all chanting and subside into it. In quietness, enjoy to the best of your capacity.
author: Sri M

text: When there is such an aspirant, who's only goal is to find the Absolute Truth and not be interested in anything else or cannot be tempted away from it, then the Guru automatically comes or finds them.
author: Sri M

text: Finding out about yourself means examining yourself thoroughly in all aspects, what you really are, how you relate to others etc. Until you understand where you are in the changing circumstances, you cannot really make any progress.
author: Sri M

text: In this path on the spiritual journey, there are no airplane and jet plane routes. Hard work is required.
author: Sri M

text: It is a question of the mind, what is my most important priority? Am I ready to practice my spiritual discipline no matter what happens, no matter even in the physical world if I have some loss, am I still ready to practice? When this happens then the acceleration is fast.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind becomes quiet and calm, it will have a reflection on the physical body also in general.
author: Sri M

text: How do you sustain in your sadhana? Through practice. Keep it as your priority and keep practicing regularly. And one day if you are not feeling nice, it is dull and nothing is happening, don't stop. Keep doing. One day it will subside and it will come back to normal.
author: Sri M

text: Even though the methods followed may be same, for each person the spiritual awakening is unique.
author: Sri M

text: Competition and comparison in the spiritual field is a very dangerous thing. We need to be free of that.
author: Sri M

text: In the spiritual field your experience should be completely original for you, as it should be, because we are all from different backgrounds, we have all passed through different births, we have had so many experiences in our past, if you believe, if you don't, it's okay.
author: Sri M

text: Be original, be your own experience.
author: Sri M

text: However much we may advance in whichever field scientifically, the human element of keeping a human being happy and grounded, and not destroyed by negative forces, should always remain uppermost in your mind.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever you do, however much you advance, use the scientific tools for the good of the world. Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah - May the whole world be happy. Let that not go out of our minds.
author: Sri M

text: When churning happens, the first thing that comes out is not amrit. Halahal visha, the great poison comes out first. Only after the poison gets exhausted, then amrit comes out.
author: Sri M

text: The most intelligent person begins to understand that there is a limit to our intelligence and there are things which are beyond our intelligence because we have a limited capacity.
author: Sri M

text: Pranayama means following the regulations or regulating the prana. Prana is life energy which flows through so many channels in our system and shvasa is breath. Controlling the breath directly affects the prana. So it is pranayama.
author: Sri M

text: If you are exploring consciousness, we cannot do it through artificial intelligence. AI itself is going to show us that if you are looking for pure consciousness, it cannot be found through any intelligence or artificial intelligence. Even ordinary intelligence cannot find it.
author: Sri M

text: Neti Neti - It is not this, it is not this, Shankara said in his philosophy. This process can be speeded up through understanding, with intelligence, natural, human or artificial. But what it is, the moment ‘I’ enters into the picture, it is not.
author: Sri M

text: When the ordinary little ego dissolves, the consciousness is revealed as the all-pervading reality.
author: Sri M

text: Intelligence in Sankhya is called buddhi , mind is called manas . Manas and buddhi are related to each other through the sthoola sharira, to the physical body, then there is also the sukshma sharira, which is the subtle body, and there is atman. So even buddhi, however much it expands, is not atman.
author: Sri M

text: According to yogic system, there are many nadis in the system, but the three main nadis are the left one, Ida, right one is Pingala and the central one is Sushumna.
author: Sri M

text: If you go a little deeper, you realize that the world you see is basically a projection of our minds.
author: Sri M

text: The teaching of the Gita is to not only discover the inner essence of your being, but also to act.
author: Sri M

text: Shakti that you worship for nine days as Navratri resides in your body, in your psycho-physical system, in the mooladhara as the Tripura Sundari , Rajarajeshwari and the whole of the practice of Tantra is to win over this Devi and take her carefully to the sahasrara where she meets her Lord who is always sitting. When this happens then the ecstasy of Saundarya happens and the Yogi is no longer an ordinary human being.
author: Sri M

text: The first thing required for anybody who takes up the practice of Sri Vidya - worship of Devi, is humility. No ego and extreme devotion so that you desire nothing but the Devi.
author: Sri M

text: The Energy and the Power that is manifested all over the world, right from the energy that you see in a tiny amoeba that moves, gets its food and eats it , is a constantly renewing force, which is also called Para Shakti. It is the highest power!
author: Sri M

text: What is pleasant may not be good. And what is good may not always be pleasant. Therefore, Tapasya means I hold on to the good - what is good for your progress, no matter how unpalatable it is for the time being.
author: Sri M

text: Whenever you say Shakti/ energy, in the Indian tradition, it is represented and symbolized as feminine. In the macrocosm nothing can function without energy. This shakti, fortunately for us, resides in every human being, man or woman, in the form of the Devi known as the Kula-Kundalini Devi.
author: Sri M

text: Yogis, Vedantins and the ancient teachers say that joy has nothing to do with what you get and what you do not get. It has nothing to do with your life's plus and minus. Your true essence is full of joy. The moment you begin to tune yourself with that, you are slowly beginning to free yourself from sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: Patience is of great importance. If you are impatient, any kind of meditation will not work because it takes time. You need to look into it carefully and do what you can do.
author: Sri M

text: Energy – once its work of creation, preservation, and destruction is done – still remains whole. The whole Cosmos is spun out of this energy or Shakti, which keeps working tirelessly and yet remains unaltered.
author: Sri M

text: That Absolute energy, in manifestation or movement, when it begins to work, is called Shakti. When it is in its potential form, absolutely at rest, without a single movement – That completeness is Shiva, the Absolute Being.
author: Sri M

text: When the energy in us wakes up, then our consciousness is lifted from the ordinary to the extraordinary. From getting caught-up in little, little trinkets, we reach for the treasure. From enjoying little joys, we go to the source of all enjoyment. When you touch the source of all enjoyment, then you are free. No more bound.
author: Sri M

text: Person who practices yoga should be ready to change his habits, even if he enjoys it, into something that is less enjoyable, maybe for the time being and therefore it is a Tapasya.
author: Sri M

text: Sahaja Samadhi doesn't mean easy Samadhi. It means, that state where even in normal times, even though you are functioning, deep down your mind is still in that state.
author: Sri M

text: Freedom from sorrow means to have joy. When you have joy you don't have sorrow anymore.
author: Sri M

text: Change has to be urgent. If I say now I'll do like this, but after 10 years, then I will change. Change will never happen. If you need to change, you have to change now. And if you change now, you will have to suffer various other factors. That suffering is called Tapasya.
author: Sri M

text: Swadhyaya has two meanings. One is to study the scriptures and the textbooks relating to your yogic journey or philosophical journey intently by yourself. It also means studying your own self.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga believes that the prana that functions inside your system can be controlled and used as and when and where you like to use. And the rate of breathing has a deep connection to your state of mind. That is the whole science of pranayama.
author: Sri M

text: Every human being is seeking something. You may call it peace, happiness, fulfillment, or bliss. These are only different terms. The mind is always trying to become complete. If only you turned around and looked, the completeness is already in existence within us.
author: Sri M

text: The source from which the entire universe has come is by itself Poorna, complete.
author: Sri M

text: Love is all that is required. All arguments and discussions fail to reach the unlimited. Only love does.
author: Sri M

text: The darkness of ignorance must go before one sees the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: The Avadhootas and Mastans are said to be a category of spiritually advanced beings who, by virtue of their communion with Unconditional Truth, have freed themselves from all conditions imposed upon human beings by so called civilized society.
author: Sri M

text: If you say that I depend on God or the Supreme Being and ask for help to fend yourself from the disasters that happen to you and not give up. That is the best way to move forward. Surrender and hard work both have to go together especially in spiritual life.
author: Sri M

text: The way of exploring or understanding consciousness is different from linear understanding of objects. Anyone who knows cannot say ‘I know' because when you know, you have no ‘I' left. The conditioned ‘l' has dissolved. So then who knows?
author: Sri M

text: For satsang there is no need to have a number of people.. It can be one, two, or a thousand. Most important thing is how much is understood. Are we listening and allowing it to go out from the other ear and go back and do the same thing? Or are we allowing what is being heard to sink into the mind so that it works at some point?
author: Sri M

text: When you see spiritual traits appear in somebody at quite a young age and sometimes you see that they don't even have a guide or a teacher, you can be rest assured they have spent many lives in sadhana and finally have come there. We cannot imitate that.
author: Sri M

text: The most important thing is sincerity and one pointed attention to the goal that you seek. It has to be the first priority.
author: Sri M

text: One has to be patient. Each person moves and progresses on the spiritual path at a different pace. Why? Because we have all come from different backgrounds, not only in this life, but also in previous lives. Therefore, different ways have to be adopted and the time taken will also be different. be negated any more.
author: Sri M

text: In this life you have to be intelligent and logical and sometimes you should plan what you are trying to do and stick to the plan. However, don't forget Dharma. Do not do anything that will cause injury or unhappiness to others.
author: Sri M

text: You are keeping the room in order: sweeping it, cleaning it, sweeping off the cobwebs, opening the windows, pulling the curtains, you are ready. Then, infinite patience is required. The breeze is definitely going to blow in. When it will come, nobody knows. When it comes, it comes in a flash. That is why all this preparation is necessary. Otherwise, when the breeze of understanding comes, our windows and doors are shut. Sadhana opens these out.
author: Sri M

text: Being spiritual doesn't mean changing your robe or having any weird hairstyle. You can be normal like anybody else, work, look after your families, do your work sincerely as truthfully as you can in this world. There is no need for any special paraphernalia to do that.
author: Sri M

text: If you have a spiritual goal and if you are moving forward, hold on to that. Ask God for help and keep moving. If you fall once, maybe you are not doing the right thing. Maybe there are lessons to be learned. Make that failure a stepping stone and move forward. Don't lose confidence. Keep at it. One day you will get it.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya is not a guarantee that you are all going to attain Moksha. It has been projected that Kriya is a jet plane. There is no jet plane path. Hard work and dedication is required, so please get free of that illusion.
author: Sri M

text: Bhava or Bhakti is a spontaneous feeling that arises in the heart. If you think that Bhakti can be cultivated, it's not possible. Anything you cultivate is not original. It is your own cultivation, your creation.
author: Sri M

text: If any of your sadhana is making you a totally feelingless, heartless person, abandon it. That's not sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: ​​Just as you apply your entire energy and mind to building up a bank balance, if you apply it to finding Liberation, you will find it. Believe me, you can lead a normal life while working, when you have found it. However, If you want to fully dedicate your life to understanding the Truth, it might be necessary to give up things and lead a life of solitude. But once it is found, you still can live in this world and work. The work will be there but it won't be self-centered. It will be for others.
author: Sri M

text: A sadhak should persist and not give up on the negative side of one's personality. On the other hand, to support that, you need to surrender to the Supreme being. It should be a mind that asks for help, but refuses to bow down and cut down one's efforts and moves forward.
author: Sri M

text: Surrender as well as hard work have to go together, especially in spiritual life.
author: Sri M

text: The purpose of life is not merely to make money or to build houses. It is to find true happiness. Once you start pursuing the spiritual and you begin to feel happiness in the inner then all the outer problems that happen to all of us will have no effect on you. You will sail through happily.
author: Sri M

text: All human beings have some problems. But if you are spiritual, you also get the energy and the perseverance to go through them and come out unscathed.
author: Sri M

text: The spiritual seeker is one who persists, so we have to persist.
author: Sri M

text: On the spiritual journey, adopt all methods possible so that you don't fall off from the path and continue to stick to that no matter what temptations and what troubles come to you. But please don't think that because you have become spiritual you will have problems. Everybody has problems.
author: Sri M

text: Love is not something that exists only when the body exists. The body has to go inevitably. But love is an immaterial thing that is a part of our soul which never dies even when the body dies. If you keep this concept in mind, not only will we learn to love in this life, but also when we leave the body, we will go with a feeling of affection and love rather than fear, distress and anger. Then there is no fear of death.
author: Sri M

text: Why do we want to learn a technique or a mantra or want to be initiated into spiritual practice? What are we seeking? What is it that is within us that seeks to fulfill itself? So it must be that we are not fulfilled. We may be materially fulfilled but then also we are not fulfilled because we are seeking.
author: Sri M

text: If you want something which gives you complete satisfaction and fulfillment, no matter what you have or what you don't have in the external world, then you are seeking the Truth. And once it is touched, you begin to understand the meaning of fulfillment.
author: Sri M

text: Upanishads are also called Aranayakas. End of the other portions of the Veda. The Sanskrit word for end is Anta. So they are known as Veda-Anta. When the Truths of the Upanishads are understood, it's finished. There is nothing more to be understood. This is also another reason why it is called Anta.
author: Sri M

text: You can only go as close as possible to the Truth. You cannot become the Truth, because as long as ‘you’ are there, there is no Truth. When ‘I am’ is gone, there is the Truth. ‘I’ is burnt off like going close to the sun.
author: Sri M

text: If that Truth is there and I am here, I need to go towards it. But what we are looking for is here, there and everywhere. Tad dure tad vadantike - It's far and yet so near. Isha vasyam idam sarvam . It pervades everything.
author: Sri M

text: Shake up your ordinary process of thinking and say, maybe there is something here which you seek, but only when all seeking stops, it is there. When all movement of the mind reaching out ends, then what is left? The seeker in his true sense with no effort and the seeker is the sought.
author: Sri M

text: Truth is Truth, doesn't matter where it comes from. The appearance of the teacher is not important. What is being taught is more important.
author: Sri M

text: Sleep is a great equalizer. We feel rejuvenated after a good night's sleep because we are not aware that we exist. Only when I am aware that I exist, do I have the problems. I am bound, I want to be free. When I don't exist, you don't exist. So we need sleep for complete rest. But there is a witness even in deep sleep.
author: Sri M

text: Everybody likes to enjoy themselves. But we think that enjoyment comes only from outside. It is within, self-sufficient bliss which is called Satchitananda in the Vedanta.
author: Sri M

text: When all the vrittis of the mind are completely removed, then what remains is a state that is very clear. You reach the essence of your being, and see the witness that witnesses everything but is not part of anything. This is the aim of yoga.
author: Sri M

text: The mind's character is of sticking to the past and not letting go of it. So it practically prevents the present from coming in. And what is the present? The Truth.
author: Sri M

text: If we can even start practicing letting go in daily life, and not simply sit down every day and say Aham Brahmasmi, Tattvam Asi, you are actually moving towards the Truth of Vedanta.
author: Sri M

text: Where one is totally absorbed in That and one knows that any amount of intellectual understanding is not going to help, heart to heart connection is required. This what you call Bhakti and it cannot be cultivated.
author: Sri M

text: These are only two ways by which Bhakti, devotion can happen. It happens spontaneously. You get this overwhelming feeling that the joy is in the Lord and in nothing else or when you are in contact with someone who has experienced it, it might seep in. There are no other ways.
author: Sri M

text: The most intelligent person very soon discovers the limitations of the intellect. The average intelligent man does not discover it. He is very proud of his intelligence. But a person who is truly intelligent soon discovers the limitedness of his intelligence.
author: Sri M

text: All the rational framework that we set up is based on the inputs or the data collected through our five senses. Nobody has more than that. These instruments of perception, the panchendriyas are very limited and colored in their inputs. Therefore when you build up an intellectual blueprint based on this data, it is bound to be incomplete or in many cases wrong.
author: Sri M

text: Universal love is beyond the mind and the brain. When we are so overwhelmed that the mind refuses to work, then you are absorbed in that. This can happen through being so selfless that the self doesn't remain anymore. But it has to happen. It is not concocted. All you can do is prepare the conditions which are proper so that it is possible that it will happen. Beyond that we have no control.
author: Sri M

text: It's only when something difficult happens and when some sorrow strikes that the mind begins to think about higher things. Otherwise, you are always hunky-dory. Nobody thinks.
author: Sri M

text: Music is a link from the world of language and its contradictions, to the world of unity of the heart where you don't require any discrimination in any language. So the root of this knowledge, this understanding is the Sama Veda.
author: Sri M

text: Richness need not mean the bank balance. Richness is to do with the mind. How rich it is.
author: Sri M

text: A beautiful statement in Kenopanishad, yanmanasā na manute yenāhurmano matam | tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate || That means that which even the mind cannot understand. So through knowledge how can you Knowledge is mind. But because of which the mind owes its awareness to or consciousness to, that alone is the Supreme Truth. Nothing that you worship here.
author: Sri M

text: The practical meaning of Self-Realization is to know your own self as you are, not project that I am a spark of the Supreme Being. We don't really know. So first you have to study yourself.
author: Sri M

text: Kaivalya comes from the root word Kevalam, which means only one. In Kaivalya , the yogi realizes that there is only one Purusha , spiritual being, (nothing to do with gender). What appears as distinct and different are the projections of the mind.
author: Sri M

text: The world is an illusion and the supreme reality is only Brahman. You can say that but you cannot realize that. You need a mind which is clear of all impurities and distractions.
author: Sri M

text: Without knowing where you are going, if you start a spiritual practice, it is likely that you might run into trouble. You are largely walking on uncharted territory. So it is necessary to know what is the need for doing it. Otherwise, you are just breathing in and out, it means nothing.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is free of distractions, absolutely silent, it becomes like a mirror that reflects only the Atman. You may also call it Purusha, in the language of the Yoga Darshana.
author: Sri M

text: OM is pure sound, pranava. It is called pranava because it is life-giving, prana. It gives you the first incentive of life. It is the beginning of all life.
author: Sri M

text: The witness is the same. The states keep changing. So the only reality is the witness and not the states that keep changing and that reality is your true being.
author: Sri M

text: Deep sleep, Sushupti is a state of sleep where there are no dreams. It may be very short. It is in this state that you actually recover and rejuvenate. This is because there is no inner cognition of who I am. There is no outer cognition of the world. Both do not exist, and therefore there is a blissful sleep.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya Yoga is a technique or a method by which step by step you can divert your mind from distractions, bring them to one place and take it straight to the higher levels of understanding.
author: Sri M

text: When the third eye or the ajna chakra is activated and the kundalini energy reaches the ajna , the mind understands the reality behind all illusion. Then all illusions are burnt to ashes and this is the last but one step towards Moksha .
author: Sri M

text: If acute desire to be free of suffering arises in a human mind, that mind need not be extraordinarily intellectual. It can be just an ordinary person with that desire; then one can completely direct oneself towards that which one can be free.
author: Sri M

text: As your feelings become more and more subtle, deeper centers of the human mind open up to form a link to that which is beyond the ordinary mind.
author: Sri M

text: True consciousness means to go beyond all images. Not images that you see around you but ones that we build up in our minds. It is because of these that we get hurt, our ego goes up and we have all the problems.
author: Sri M

text: If you have faith in an infinite Supreme Being, put all your heart into what you want to do or achieve.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is open, and when there is the great desire to achieve something then the channels for achieving it are opened.
author: Sri M

text: All things about spiritual matters boil down to your relationships, day to day. We can sit at home and meditate for hours but when we come out and we are still the same, it does not work.
author: Sri M

text: You have a slate and you write on it. Every time you write on it, if you want to write anything else, you have to rub it off. So in matters of inner exploration, the most important thing is to keep your slate clean.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t unnecessarily complicate life with too many things. That does not mean that when you speak the truth you have to be blunt. There are sweet ways of speaking the truth.
author: Sri M

text: Does freedom happen in stages? I would say, It’s like the wheel; the network of illusion is gradually lifted as one goes deeper and deeper into understanding one’s own self, one’s own mind.
author: Sri M

text: People usually think spiritual realisation is for free. This is not true. ‘He who giveth, shall receive’. By giveth, it does not mean giving money to somebody. It is more than that. There is nothing on this earth or in heaven that can be achieved without sacrificing something – that’s why it is called a ‘sacrifice’. If you sacrifice, you receive.
author: Sri M

text: Jesus Christ in the Bible said, ‘Every hill shall be brought low and every valley shall be filled’. So when you are in that stage of low, you should think I am a valley now I am going to be filled at some point. And when I am high up, I must understand that I am a hill, I could be brought down anytime. That balance must be maintained.
author: Sri M

text: In the present circumstances of your capacity of your brain, it is not possible to understand Brahma Vidya. So, you need to prepare your mind now to understand the concept of Brahma Vidya and at some point, expand it enough to receive the experience of Brahma Vidya.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga Shastra is necessary. Gita has 18 chapters, each chapter is called a Yoga. It need not necessarily mean the Yoga that you practice, the Yoga of Ashtangas. It could mean any approach to understanding which will open up your mind.
author: Sri M

text: The practice of Yoga or any sadhana is how to open these windows and doors, so that you can get a glimpse of what the all-pervading Brahman, reality is. This is the whole scope of the practice of Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: Freedom is Mukti, Vedantins call it Moksha, Yogis call it Kaivalya, Buddhists call it Nirvana and the Sufis call it Fana fil Haq, which means everything is finished except the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: If you look closely, all through our lives, we go through periods of bondage and periods of freedom. But when we say Mukti from the spiritual point of view, it means ultimate freedom.
author: Sri M

text: There is a way to be free while still living in this world, performing your duties, doing what you want and yet be free. Our own mind is the tool. It's the mind that binds and it's the mind that sets free. But first we need to realise that we are bound. If I think I am free, then there is no need to be free.
author: Sri M
